ai.literal: Even if they exceed, even if they decrease, disease will cause, (those) which the authors of treatises, wind beginning with, reckoned as three.
ai.translation: If the three humors reckoned by medical experts, beginning with wind, either exceed or fall short of their proper measure, they will cause disease.
ai.modern: மருத்துவ நூலோர் வளி (காற்று) முதலாக எண்ணிய மூன்று பொருள்களும் (வளி, பித்தம், ஐயம்) அளவுக்கு அதிகமானாலும் அல்லது குறைந்தாலும் உடலுக்கு நோயை உண்டாக்கும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet introduces the fundamental principle of traditional medicine regarding the three bodily humors: wind (vatha), bile (pitha), and phlegm (kapha). The poet refers to them as the 'three things reckoned by experts, beginning with wind'. Health is maintained when these three elements exist in perfect balance. If any of these three humors either exceeds its natural proportion or falls below it, the imbalance disrupts the body's harmony and causes disease.

ai.literal: Medicine as will not be needed for the body, if one eats after carefully ensuring that what was previously eaten has been digested.
ai.translation: No medicine is needed for the body if one eats only after ensuring that what was previously consumed has been fully digested.
ai.modern: முன் உண்ட உணவு செரித்ததை உறுதி செய்து கொண்டு அதன் பிறகு உண்டால், உடம்பிற்கு மருந்து என்று ஒன்று தேவையில்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights a fundamental principle of preventive health. It states that the human body does not require any external medicine if a person regulates their eating habits. The key is to wait until the previously consumed food ('aruntiyatu') is completely digested ('aṟṟatu') before eating again. By carefully observing this digestion process ('pōṟṟi') and eating only when the body is ready ('uṇiṉ'), one maintains natural health, making medicine ('maruntu') entirely unnecessary.

ai.literal: If digested, completely having known, eat; that is the way for him who obtained a body to sustain it for a long time.
ai.translation: Once the food previously eaten is fully digested, assure yourself of it and then eat; that is the way for one who has obtained a body to preserve it for a long time.
ai.modern: முன் உண்ட உணவு செரித்ததை முழுமையாக அறிந்து உண்ண வேண்டும்; அதுவே உடம்பைப் பெற்றவன் அதனை நீண்ட காலம் செலுத்தும் வழியாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the fundamental rule of health and longevity. One must eat only after ensuring that the previous meal has been completely digested. The phrase 'அற அறிந்து' emphasizes that one must be absolutely certain of this digestion before consuming more. Following this simple discipline is described as the ultimate way ('ஆறு') to sustain the physical body ('உடம்பு') and ensure a long, healthy life.

ai.literal: That which was digested having known, holding fast (to this rule), things that are not disagreeable let one eat, thoroughly having become hungry.
ai.translation: Ascertaining that the previous meal is fully digested, and holding fast to this rule, eat only compatible foods after becoming thoroughly hungry.
ai.modern: முன்பு உண்ட உணவு செரித்ததை அறிந்து, அதனை உறுதியாகக் கடைப்பிடித்து, உடலுக்கு மாறுபாடு இல்லாத உணவுகளை நன்கு பசித்த பிறகு உண்ண வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet outlines the fundamental rules of eating for maintaining good health. First, one must ensure that the previously consumed food is completely digested ('அற்றது அறிந்து'). Second, one must wait until a clear, strong hunger is felt ('துவரப் பசித்து'). Third, one must eat only those foods that are compatible with one's body and do not conflict with each other ('மாறு அல்ல'). Adhering firmly to these guidelines ('கடைப்பிடித்து') prevents disease and eliminates the need for medicine.

ai.literal: If one eats, with moderation, food that is without incompatibility, there is no harm to life.
ai.translation: If a person eats with moderation food that is compatible with their body, there will be no harm to their life.
ai.modern: உடலுக்கு ஒத்துப்போகாத தன்மை இல்லாத உணவை, அளவுடன் கட்டுப்படுத்தி உண்டால், உயிருக்கு எந்தத் துன்பமும் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights two essential rules of healthy eating: compatibility and moderation. The term 'māṟupāṭu illāta uṇṭi' refers to food that does not conflict with one's physical constitution or with other foods eaten together. The phrase 'maṟuttu uṇṇiṉ' advises eating with self-restraint, rejecting excess even when the food is agreeable. By choosing compatible food and eating it in moderate quantities, one can prevent illness and ensure a long, healthy life.

ai.literal: Knowing moderation, with the one who eats, like pleasure will stand, with the one of excessively great food, disease.
ai.translation: Just as health and pleasure abide with the one who eats with moderation, so does disease dwell with the glutton who overeats excessively.
ai.modern: அளவறிந்து உண்பவனிடத்தில் இன்பம் நிலைத்து நிற்பது போல, மிக அதிகமாக உண்பவனிடத்தில் நோய் நிலைத்து நிற்கும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses a striking comparison to emphasize the importance of moderate eating. It states that just as health and happiness (இன்பம்) constantly dwell with a person who understands the proper limit (இழிவு) of their food intake and eats accordingly, disease (நோய்) will permanently reside with the glutton who consumes excessively large amounts of food (கழிபேர் இரையான்). The word 'இழிவு' here refers to the lower or moderate limit of food, indicating eating less than one's full capacity. The poet contrasts 'இன்பம்' (pleasure/health) and 'நோய்' (disease) as constant companions to the moderate eater and the overeater respectively.

ai.literal: If one, disregarding the measure of their digestive fire, without discerning, eats excessively, disease will arise without limit.
ai.translation: If a person eats excessively without discerning and disregarding the measure of their digestive fire, diseases will arise without limit.
ai.modern: தன் பசித் தீயின் அளவை ஆராய்ந்து அறியாமல், ஒருவன் மிகுதியாக உண்டால், அவனுக்கு நோய்கள் எல்லையின்றி உண்டாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the importance of eating according to one's digestive capacity, referred to metaphorically as 'tī' (fire). The word 'teriyāṉ' refers to a person who does not analyze or understand this capacity. When such a person eats excessively ('perituṇṇiṉ'), ignoring the limits of their digestive fire, it leads to severe consequences. The result is that diseases ('nōy') will arise in them without any limit ('aḷaviṉṟi'). Thus, moderation based on personal digestive strength is key to preventing endless illnesses.

ai.literal: Disease having investigated, disease's root cause having investigated, that which mitigates way having investigated, so as to succeed, act.
ai.translation: Diagnose the disease, diagnose its root cause, investigate the proper method to cure it, and then administer the treatment effectively.
ai.modern: நோயை ஆராய்ந்து, நோயின் மூல காரணத்தை ஆராய்ந்து, அதைத் தணிக்கும் வழியை ஆராய்ந்து, அது பலிக்கும்படி செய்ய வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet outlines the systematic approach required for medical treatment. First, the physician must identify the specific disease. Second, they must investigate its root cause rather than just treating the symptoms. Third, they must find the correct method or remedy to cure it. Finally, they must execute the treatment in a way that ensures success. The repetition of the word 'நாடி' (having investigated) emphasizes that careful diagnosis and inquiry must precede any action.

ai.literal: The patient's measure, and the disease's measure, and the time, the learned physician, having considered, should act.
ai.translation: The learned physician should carefully consider the patient's physical condition, the severity of the disease, and the appropriate season before administering treatment.
ai.modern: நோயாளி உடைய உடலின் வலிமை மற்றும் வயதின் அளவையும், நோயின் தன்மையின் அளவையும், தகுந்த காலத்தையும் கற்றுணர்ந்த மருத்துவர் ஆராய்ந்து பார்த்துச் சிகிச்சை செய்ய வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet outlines the essential diagnostic steps a trained physician must take before treating a patient. First, 'uṟṟāṉ aḷavu' refers to assessing the patient's age, strength, and constitution. Second, 'piṇi aḷavu' means evaluating the severity, type, and stage of the disease. Third, 'kālam' refers to considering the season, climate, and time of day, which affect both the body and the potency of medicine. Only after thoroughly analyzing these three factors should the learned practitioner ('kaṟṟāṉ') proceed with the treatment ('ceyal').

ai.literal: The patient, the healer, the medicine, and the attendant who goes near, thus, of those categories, four parts indeed is medicine.
ai.translation: The patient, the physician, the medicine, and the attendant—medicine consists of these four parts, each having its own role.
ai.modern: நோயாளி, குணப்படுத்தும் மருத்துவர், மருந்து, அருகில் இருந்து உதவும் உதவியாளர் என்று அந்த நான்கு வகைப் பாகங்களைக் கொண்டதுதான் மருத்துவ முறை ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet outlines the four essential components that constitute the entire system of medicine or healing. It lists them as: the patient (உற்றவன்), the physician (தீர்ப்பான்), the medicine itself (மருந்து), and the caregiver or attendant (உழைச்செல்வான்). For a successful cure, all four elements must function together effectively. The word 'உழைச்செல்வான்' literally means 'one who goes near', highlighting the crucial role of the nurse or assistant who administers the treatment and cares for the patient.
